const report = `# TokenEconomizer and Codex token audit

**4 November 2026 IST · EOD Charting Platform · TokenEconomizer 0.1.0**

## Runtime and savings

**PASS for hook operation. FAIL for complete, reliable token accounting.** The Codex plugin is enabled, its local Python core resolves, and the installed hook manifest registers SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop and SessionEnd. Start and end markers, recorded prompts, 500 tool calls across 122 distinct guard turn summaries, and 19 unique session folds show the lifecycle ran. Recovery folding can also run at the next start, so a ledger row alone cannot establish SessionEnd delivery. Two folds report \`transcript unreadable\` and their session IDs have no matching retained rollout in the inspected roots. Four other folds have no usage. The committed SQLite log snapshot had no matching hook warning/error rows. Its active WAL was excluded, so this is neither a complete failure history nor a separate end-to-end attestation for Desktop and CLI. The CLI launcher and source were inspected without invoking \`te status\`, which can update plugin state.

**Verified savings: none quantified.** Global configuration is enabled with \`shadow=false\`. The repository overrides \`toolprune\` to \`propose\`. Stored state lists three proposals across 13 sessions and 127 prompts, all 19 session rows record an empty applied list, no plugin applied-denylist receipt exists, and the repository has no \`.codex/config.toml\`. This verifies zero recorded TokenEconomizer capability removals for this project. Ledger injection totals are zero and no current injection file was present. The ~98% cache-hit share is Codex telemetry and cannot be attributed to TokenEconomizer.

**LoopGuard ran and incurred overhead.** It recorded two cumulative-backstop nudges at 41 and 29 tool calls, and an escalation at 69 calls after the 41-call nudge. The records show a 23-call threshold and envelopes of about 9.4 and 9.0. The escalation labeled \`abort\` delivered a notice. The handler leaves stopping to the user. The retained judge verdicts inspected were negative for stuck, and the intervention labels identify the deterministic backstop. The records cannot show whether the nudges improved outcomes or prevented more work. Sixteen distinct judge jobs logged **235,569 effective-token equivalents**, around 0.66% of the plugin's recorded execution-plus-overhead total. That share is ledger-relative and excludes any unrecorded work. The separate judge rows explain why zero judge usage in the turn/session summaries does not imply zero overhead.

## Reconciliation

| Metric | Reconciled local rollout sample |
|---|---:|
| Input including cache reads | 433,055,302 |
| Cached input | 424,402,688 (98.0%) |
| Uncached input, input minus cached | 8,652,614 |
| Output including reasoning where supported by the counters | 1,458,853 |
| Reasoning output, reported separately | 555,638 |
| Input plus output | 434,514,155 |
| Host-reported total | 434,776,114 |
| Host total minus input plus output | 261,959 |

The V1 report shows 885.02M raw total. V2 shows 429,474,049 in the host total field and excludes 456,522,388 of initial cumulative overhang. That overhang can contain inherited or already-accounted usage. The difference between V1 and V2 is an accounting correction. The V2 host total also exceeds its input-plus-output sum, so these measures are tracked separately. The residual in the refreshed sample remains unclassified. In a directly matched rollout, output already contains reasoning, as input plus output equals the host total despite nonzero reasoning. Adding the reasoning field to output again would overstate that session.

The refresh streamed 37 active and archived rollout files, matching 29 files to the exact project working directory and 28 distinct session IDs. The sole matching archive had no usage records. One repeated session ID spans two active files with disjoint observed usage timestamp ranges and separately initialized counters. Both segments contribute. Within files, 16 repeated cumulative snapshots were skipped. No exact cross-file event duplicates, within-file resets, or last-versus-delta mismatches were observed. Cross-session overlap with rewritten timestamps, missing rollouts, alternate roots, and incomplete active tails remain possible. The refresh counted 2,294 distinct usage snapshots with a nonzero metric and 1,992 tool calls. These counts cover different event types. The V2 files were reused for output-size rankings, and the refresh was limited to the metadata necessary to check overlap, current totals, and compaction.

**TokenEconomizer effective tokens** are weighted fresh-input equivalents. All 13 priced folds used fallback weights of 1× fresh input, 0.10× cache reads, 1.25× cache creation and 6× output. Their recorded components were 4,240,253 fresh input, 240,312,576 cache reads, zero cache creation and 1,185,616 plugin output, giving **35,385,207 effective equivalents** before judge overhead. The plugin takes each selected rollout's last cumulative counter, counts snapshots as requests, and adds reasoning to output. For sample \`01a1a02e\`, the ledger counted 62,679 output versus the rollout's 49,751, a difference equal to its 12,928 reasoning tokens. That inflates this fold's weighted total by 77,568 equivalents under its fallback curve. The smaller fold coverage, potential inherited counters, and fallback weights make ledger totals unsuitable as an independent raw usage check or an account allowance estimate. Local files provide no authoritative mapping to subscription limits, credits, or reset windows.

## Ranked consumption drivers and recommendations

1. **Repeated large contexts across long tool-driven turns. Highest likely impact.** The top three sessions account for 225.35M input-plus-output tokens, about 52% of the refreshed sample, and made 386, 231 and 161 tool calls. V2's largest individual calls reached roughly 452k raw tokens. Batch independent reads and use tight search scopes and explicit stop conditions. Low risk when dependent checks remain sequential. For scale only, avoiding ten comparable 300k-input requests would avoid 3M raw input tokens. At the observed 98% cache mix and plugin fallback weights, that is about 354k input equivalents before output, replacement calls or cache changes. It is a scenario, not a forecast.
2. **Oversized tool results and context growth. High likely impact.** V2 logged 1,605,472 and 701,896 characters in its two largest tool results. Use bounded excerpts, counts, and sanitized failure summaries. Keep full evidence local when needed and retrieve exact slices. Character counts cannot establish model-visible size after host truncation or quantify savings. Nine compaction records appeared in seven sessions. In the most expensive session, adjacent nonzero inputs around two compactions fell from 397,580 to 60,828 and from 449,305 to 139,580. This shows shorter observed inputs after compaction. The cost of summarization, any cache loss and later regrowth remain unisolated. Use concise handoffs at natural phase boundaries. Premature thread resets may discard context and warm cache.
3. **Output and reasoning. Smaller raw share, potentially material under weighted accounting.** Reported reasoning is about 38% of output. Reserve deeper reasoning for work that needs it and compare task quality before using a lower effort setting. The available sample does not isolate the effect of model or effort from task difficulty.
4. **Plugin changes. Benefit unproven and capability risk higher.** Correct and validate accounting before relying on the ledger for savings. Keep proposals advisory pending schema measurements and task coverage. Measure LoopGuard's judge overhead and false interventions separately before tuning it. Missing tools, unnecessary interruption and cache invalidation can offset gains.

## Controlled A/B plan

With separate authorization, use disposable identical checkouts and isolated Codex profiles, never the live project settings or data. Pin the repo commit, Codex build, model and effort, prompt, tools, permissions, external-data fixture, and acceptance checks. Use fresh sessions and separate cold and warmed-cache cohorts. Randomize run order and repeat paired tasks across small, long-context and retry-heavy cases. Run the first comparison with plugin off versus the current settings. Isolate LoopGuard and each proposed capability change in subsequent arms. Verify actual tool availability and measure first-call input at equivalent cache conditions.

Capture per-request counter components, rollout lineage, compaction, tool calls, completed work, elapsed time and separately identified sidecalls. Count all sidecall costs, retries and recovery work. Compare medians, paired variation and task success, retaining runs that fail or time out. Use raw fields as primary outcomes and document any weighting as a secondary analysis. Set success and maximum spend criteria before running. The current evidence lacks matched controls, a measured prompt-schema delta, complete hook/sidecall lineage, independently verified task outcomes and authoritative allowance telemetry. No experiment was run during this audit.

## Evidence and changes

Sources were the project instructions and Git status, installed hook manifest and local core source, TokenEconomizer state, Codex active and archived rollout metadata and committed SQLite logs, and the existing sanitized V1/V2 Downloads reports. Evidence was sampled from live files and is point-in-time. Git was already dirty on \`main\` (50 modified and 28 untracked status entries). No project files, Git state, settings, hooks, plugin files or prior audit files were changed by the audit. This sanitized report is the only file written by the audit. Codex and already-enabled hooks can maintain their normal session records independently. No network, recursive Codex invocation, benchmark or project validation was run. A separately authorized accounting check and paired pilot would establish whether any optimization reduces cost at equal task quality.
`;
